title: Are these two lines parallel?
description: Two lines are cut by a transversal, and one angle at each crossing is given. A linear pair finds the corresponding angle, and the two corresponding angles are compared. Keeko doubts the answer, because the lines look parallel.
teaching_notes: One idea: parallel lines have equal corresponding angles, so unequal corresponding angles show the lines are not parallel. Watch for students who decide by how the lines look.

source: Lines l and m are cut by a transversal t, with the angles a,
video_script.why: The child uses a linear pair to find one corresponding angle and compares it with the other, to test whether two lines are parallel.
video_script.substitution: the book's own figure: lines l and m cut by a transversal t, angles a, b, d, c at the upper crossing and e, f, h, g in the same corners at the lower crossing, a is one hundred and twenty degrees and f is seventy degrees
video_script.anchor: lines l and m cut by the transversal t, with angles a, b, d, c at the upper crossing and e, f, h, g in the same corners at the lower crossing, a marked 120° and f marked 70°
video_script.wrong_move: decides that the lines are parallel by how they look, and does not compare the corresponding angles
video_script.payoff_line: Corresponding angles that are not equal mean the lines are not parallel

final_answer.value: No: the corresponding angles are 60° and 70°, which are not equal
final_answer.spoken: no, the corresponding angles are sixty degrees and seventy degrees, which are not equal

hold_back: No: the corresponding angles are 60° and 70°, which are not equal
maths_rules: a and b are a linear pair, so b = 180 - 120 = 60
b and f are corresponding angles
if l and m were parallel, b would be equal to f
b = 60 and f = 70, and 70 - 60 = 10, so b and f are not equal
so l and m are not parallel
video_script.design: One figure for the whole video. The angles b and f are filled in two colours when they are compared, and a gap of ten degrees is shown between them.

<bookmark mark='rule'/>For parallel lines, corresponding angles must be equal.
